_paths_comment: Portable paths: ${HOUFIN_DATA}/${HOUFIN_PROCESSED} expand at load (src/config_utils.py; default <repo>/data and <repo>/data/processed locally, override via env on HPC). NOTE: raw_z_dir and path_features.output_dir are the SAME directory and must be kept in sync by hand -- generate_all_path_features writes the latter, model_inputs reads the former (they consume the encoder cube + BBS produced upstream).
_model_spec_comment: Comments in this file describe THIS file's (base) values. The current HMC candidate (LA1) runs this file with an experiment overlay merged on top, which changes many values (54 km grid, rank 64, capacity_demography + coupling priors, clumped Allee with pinned n50, capacity_floor_internal, disease on survival, Veit + native departure, spin-up, single 1951 release). The as-executed model is specified in docs/model_spec/ (MODEL_SPEC.md, NOTATION.md, RESOLVED_CONFIG.json); docs/PRIORS.md gives the candidate's values beside these.
_disease_arrival_map_comment: Per-pixel first-affected-breeding-season for House Finch mycoplasmal conjunctivitis, on the model grid. Built by scripts/build_disease_arrival_map.py from the documented 1994-2006 spread history (there is no published raster). Consumed by model_inputs.py as the epizootic onset map. Under this file's default (disease_prior.target = capacity) it gates the K depression; under target = survival (the current HMC candidate LA1; docs/model_spec/) it gates the ADDED MORTALITY (the candidate overlay sets onset_gate compact_start, a 3-yr smoothstep; this file's default gate differs) and K has no disease term. See docs/PRIORS.md#disease-term.

kernel_contract._comment: The encoder supplies an uncentered 64-D Nyström feature map; model ingestion explicitly retains the first latent_dim (24 in this file) eigenfeatures to fit VRAM. Conditional on each w_scale, iid coefficients over those retained features imply Cov[H(x),H(x')|w_scale] = w_scale^2 Z_r(x)·Z_r(x'), the configured rank-r approximation to the original Ružička kernel. Truncation must be config-driven and recorded, never silent. The current candidate overrides latent_dim = 64 and readout.rank = 64 (no truncation).

dispersal._comment: Single source of truth shared by Z_disp preparation and the forward model; resolved in exactly one place, build_kernels.dispersal_spec. Do not duplicate these boundaries in code.
dispersal._radial_splits_comment: juvenile_radial_splits_km takes either an explicit list of km boundaries (start 0.0, end >=1e8) or the string "derive" for equal-mass radial bands. The pinned literals are NOT quantiles of the current kernel. See docs/PRIORS.md#radial-splits.
dispersal._kernel_source_comment: Veit & Lewis 1996 kernels: the adult and juvenile SHAPES DIFFER (0.859 vs 0.468). The current candidate's juvenile kernel is the V&L-faithful 2-D form exp(-(d/b)^a)/d (J200: b 24.937 km, 1-D mean 200 km), recorded only in the input directory's KERNEL_DISCRETISATION.json (metadata dispersal_spec still carries the older labels). See docs/PRIORS.md#dispersal-kernels.
dispersal._path_comment: Z_disp is intentionally a land-conditioned neighborhood/path summary: at each fractional displacement, water/nodata is excluded and the remaining land contribution is normalized. It is not a literal trajectory hazard through water.

age_structure_prior._comment: Resolution-invariant weak local-age-structure regularizer. We average log Beta density over land cell-years, then multiply by effective_sites, instead of treating every grid cell/year as an independent prior observation. This is a distributional belief about a representative local cell, not a prior on the domain-wide mean.

population_model._comment: Mechanistic/data-scale constants persisted into model-input metadata; no hidden grid or invasion constants in ingestion code.
population_model._scale_comment: THE GAUGE: population_scale_route_counts_per_relative_unit converts model density to the mean of a BBS route count. A sampler-conditioning choice, not biology -- the likelihood is invariant to it, EXCEPT for capacity_floor_internal (set in the current candidate), which is declared in internal units. See docs/PRIORS.md#the-gauge.
population_model._release_allee_comment: Years from the release (invasion_timestep) during which the 9 candidate release cells skip the mate-finding Allee factor. The Allee term models continental colonization (thin arrivals into a 27 km cell); released cage birds were aggregated far below grid scale, so mates did not limit them. Without this the fit inflated and concentrated the founder pulse to clear the cell-averaged threshold -- a saddle with corner-shaped modes (probe of run_17). Matches invasion_window_years. 0 restores the old behaviour. The current candidate sets 0 (no exemption; one release cell on the 54 km grid). See docs/PRIORS.md#invasion-sites.
population_model._dispersal_random_comment: Per-year Normal(0, 0.001) noise on the dispersal logit. At that scale it moves dispersal by ~0.025%; the run_18 probe found its 124 directions exactly at prior curvature and L-BFGS moved it ~3e-5. false removes the site (the model uses zeros). See docs/PRIORS.md#structural-switches.
population_model._disease_prior_comment: This file's default (disease_prior.target = capacity): the mycoplasmal-conjunctivitis effect on capacity, as a STRUCTURED hypothesis: K = K_base * (1 - severity(x) * onset_gate(x,t) * (1 - recovery(t - arrival))). The current candidate sets target = survival instead: ADDED MORTALITY m = mortality_ceiling (.8) * sigmoid(mu + b_late*dec + b_native*shape + basis*w_sev) * gate * (1 - recovery) * hill(N') on adult, juvenile-stayer and juvenile-arriver survival; K is disease-free. See docs/PRIORS.md#disease-term and src/model/age_fields.py.
population_model._capacity_level_comment: Prior on K's continental LEVEL, in expected BBS route counts, anchored on the typical OCCUPIED cell (27 km median 2.618 in this file; the current candidate uses 2.582 on the 54 km grid with alpha_k_scale 1.0, and adds capacity_floor_internal after the link). See docs/PRIORS.md#capacity-level.
population_model._allee_comment: Allee half-saturation n50 on the BBS ROUTE-COUNT scale (median-route counts; internal = counts / pop_scalar). This file's default (no aggregation_k): allee_factor = 1 - 2^(-C/n50), half released at C = n50. The current candidate uses aggregation_k = 3, per_capita = true: allee_factor = 1 - (1 + ln2*C/(3*n50))^-4, half released at C = 0.819*n50, with n50 PINNED (pinned_sites.n50_raw = -3.756179, n50 = .0231 counts). Literature comparison (Veit & Lewis 1996, birds/km2) goes through the Partners in Flight absolute bridge (1 mean-route count = .735 [.367] birds/km2), not a K-ratio transfer, and compares half-points; capacity_floor_internal is absolute (internal units) and does not follow n50. See docs/PRIORS.md#allee-effect.
population_model._initpop_comment: The t=0 (1902) native-range seed, as a FRACTION OF LOCAL FITTED CAPACITY (K before any capacity floor) rather than an absolute abundance. Read the consequence of core_fraction_of_local_capacity = 1.0 before changing it. When population_model.spinup is enabled (current candidate: 40 years at the 1902-06 mean rates, no disease, no release) this seed only starts the spin-up, and the 1902 state is the spun-up total. See docs/PRIORS.md#initial-population.
population_model._invasion_pulse_comment: The 1940 release, as a fraction of a FIXED, empirically observed, K-independent reference -- deliberately not tied to k_level or local K_base. The current candidate releases ONCE, in 1951 (timestep 49), into one cell, with invasion_pulse_prior.form = single and log_inv_total pinned at 0, so founders = global_q50_route_counts / pop_scalar (.6852/20 = .03426 internal). See docs/PRIORS.md#invasion-pulse.
population_model._invasion_sites_comment: invasion_sites = 9: the record documents one known sighting, not that it was the only release, and at 27 km the literal coordinate may not land on a valid cell. The current candidate's inputs carry 4 candidate cells and form = single uses only the first. See docs/PRIORS.md#invasion-sites.
population_model._invasion_budget_comment: With 90 free (site, year) coefficients the SHARED prior must tighten, or the term becomes a high-dimensional escape hatch. Not active when invasion_pulse_prior.form = single (current candidate). See docs/PRIORS.md#invasion-budget.

capacity_level_prior._link_switch_comment: softplus (default) or exp. At the operating point the softplus argument is ~-2.1, where softplus ~ exp, so low K costs the same under both; exp removes softplus's shrinkage of the upper tail. alpha_k's location is re-solved per link so the level median stays at target_level_median_route_counts. See docs/PRIORS.md#structural-switches.
capacity_level_prior._link_comment: K uses a SOFTPLUS link applied in DENSITY space: K_base = softplus(alpha_k + H_k [+ k_trend when enabled]), no gauge conversion around it; the slope gamma_k is fixed at 1. Under this file's default (disease_prior.target = capacity) K = K_base * (1 - disease fraction) [+ capacity_floor_internal when set]; under target = survival K = K_base [+ floor]. The current candidate has no trend (k_trend.enabled = false) and a floor of .0231039 internal. See docs/PRIORS.md#capacity-link.
capacity_level_prior._calibration_comment: target_level_median_route_counts is the belief; alpha_k's prior LOCATION is solved from it at import by age_priors._softplus_loc_for_median. See docs/PRIORS.md#capacity-calibration.

population_model._manifold_comment: Correlated weights for FOUR demographic manifolds, ordered [survival_adult, reproduction, capacity, survival_juv] -- survival_juv is APPENDED, so w_env[:,0..2] keeps its meaning for positional readers. This file's form is rank2; the current candidate uses capacity_demography (Sa, F and Sj share ONE direction f; beta_K = w_K*(r_K*f + sqrt(1-r_K^2)*g)). See docs/PRIORS.md#manifold-prior.
population_model._amplitude_comment: GP AMPLITUDE, one per manifold: w_scale_j = softplus(Normal(amplitude_loc_j, amplitude_scale_j)), so Var(beta_j) = w_scale_j^2 and H_j is a GP conditional on it. The current candidate uses amplitude_scale [1.0263, 1.0263, 1.0227, 1.0263]. See docs/PRIORS.md#gp-amplitude.

manifold_prior._form_comment: rank2 (this file: two coupled groups via communality + angle, below), exchangeable (ONE coupling rho for all four fields: beta_j = w_scale_j*(sqrt(rho)*f + sqrt(1-rho)*eps_j); rho = sigmoid(Normal(logit(coupling_target), coupling_logit_scale))), capacity_demography (current candidate: one shared direction for Sa/F/Sj, K mixed at r_K = sigmoid(N(logit .85, .15)); ignores coupling_target, target_corr_*, communality_logit_scale, angle_scale and fixed_coupling) or survival_breeding. See docs/PRIORS.md#structural-switches.

population_model._k_range_comment: REPORTING threshold only -- not an active constraint. In this file K is softplus(alpha_k + H_k + trend) with nothing bounding it below, so a collapse is meant to be VISIBLE in metrics.json:k_range rather than hidden by a clamp (when capacity_floor_internal is set, as in the current candidate, K >= that floor). 24x is +/-2 log SD of the observed occupied-cell spread (log sd 1.592, from scripts/diagnostics/bbs_abundance_quantiles.py), i.e. the fold range the data actually show; the 54 km value is 26 (exp(2 x 1.6277)). A realized range well beyond it means K is being used to explain absence that should be explained by lambda < 1.
population_model._k_trend_comment: Continental smooth time trend on K's pre-softplus argument, time-centered so alpha_k keeps the level. A SAFETY VALVE AND FAILURE DIAGNOSTIC, not a modeled mechanism. Disabled in the current candidate (k_trend.enabled = false). See docs/PRIORS.md#k-trend.

disease_prior._severity_comment: DENSITY-DEPENDENT severity: a Hill function of local carrying capacity (this file's target = capacity), because epidemics need hosts. Under target = survival (current candidate) the Hill term acts on CURRENT post-dispersal density N' and multiplies the added-mortality amplitude, with hill_n bounded to (0.5, 2.55). See docs/PRIORS.md#disease-severity.
disease_prior._ceiling_comment: Applies to target = capacity only (this file's default); under target = survival (current candidate) severity_ceiling is unused and mortality_ceiling (.8) bounds the added mortality and sets the hill_n upper bound .85*(4/.8 - 2) = 2.55. For target = capacity, severity_ceiling is LOAD-BEARING FOR IDENTIFIABILITY, not merely a bound on plausibility. K = K_base*(1 - severity(K_base)*...) must be monotone in K_base, or two different habitat qualities map to the same realized capacity. At 0.5 monotonicity holds for every n tested (min dK/dK_base = 0.100 at n=5); at 0.7 it BREAKS (slope -0.26). It also happens to match the documented ~50-60% decline, which was measured in the dense eastern populations -- exactly where this parameterization applies it. Do not raise it above ~0.6 without re-checking monotonicity.
disease_prior._mu_comment: Logit of the MODIFIER on density-dependent severity, not of the removed fraction itself: severity = severity_ceiling * sigmoid(mu + ...) * hill(K_base) (target = capacity). Under target = survival (current candidate): m = mortality_ceiling * sigmoid(mu + ...) * gate * (1 - recovery) * hill(N'), prior-median peak .8 * .8 = 64% at saturating density. See docs/PRIORS.md#disease-severity-modifier.
disease_prior._field_comment: sev_field_budget is the total regional deviation the severity field may add on the logit scale (distributed as budget/sqrt(n) per coefficient); 0.5 comfortably reaches west ~25-30% vs east ~60%. lag0_scale/lag_field_budget are YEARS of onset-timing slack, continental and regional respectively -- the arrival map is a hand-built smoothed reconstruction, so its timing is coarse both overall and regionally.
disease_prior._late_comment: Severity coefficient on decades since the EPIDEMIC'S OWN start (disease_start_year=1993), not since any cell's local arrival. See docs/PRIORS.md#disease-late-era.
disease_prior._native_comment: NATIVE-LINEAGE severity suppression, on the same dimensionless core/margin shape that seeds 1902 abundance. See docs/PRIORS.md#disease-native-resistance.
disease_prior._recovery_comment: Slowly increasing resilience after local arrival: the hit decays toward severity*(1-recovery_fraction) with an e-folding time of recovery_tau years. recovery_logit_loc=-0.5 -> prior median ~38% of the hit eventually recovered, spanning 0 to ~90%.

map._comment: Continuation begins under tight priors and progressively relaxes them at absolute optimizer steps. The standard/full run uses 300 tight + 300 intermediate + 1200 nominal-prior steps (1800 total). Boundaries are independent of TOTAL_STEPS so extending/resuming a run cannot move backward. lr_decay_steps is likewise fixed across extensions; after step 900 optimization continues at the schedule's minimum learning rate.
map._log_every_comment: Steps between '[map] step ...' progress lines on stdout (the SLURM .o log). tqdm also carries the loss, but it writes a single carriage-return-rewritten line to stderr, so a running fit's loss trajectory is otherwise invisible in the log. Override per-run with HOUFIN_MAP_LOG_EVERY; 0 disables. A profile may set its own value.

quick90._comment: Short development fit: 100 tight, 100 intermediate and 200 nominal-prior steps (400 total, per prior_relaxation below). The learning-rate decay reaches its minimum at step 300 (lr_decay_steps) and stays there for the final 100. This changes optimization only, not the final MAP objective. The name is historical -- it was a 900-step, ~90-minute profile before the schedule was compressed; it is now much shorter.

runtime._comment: Production JAX jobs require a GPU and explicitly place model inputs in VRAM. HOUFIN_MODEL_INPUT_RESIDENCY=host is experimental: lax.scan is not a true differentiable host-streaming mechanism. SLURM wrappers record nvidia-smi VRAM/utilization plus host MemAvailable/SwapFree every 30 seconds (the interval is the second positional argument to start_gpu_monitor in the .slurm files, not a config key).
